questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs of transformations commutes for every function $y = f(x)$?

options.why: Transformations along the same vertical axis do not commute in general.
Transformations along the same horizontal axis do not commute in general.

options.text: Reflection in the $y$-axis and horizontal translation
options.why: Reflection in the $y$-axis and horizontal shift both act on the $x$-axis and do not commute.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Transformations on different axes (horizontal vs vertical) are independent and commute.}$
$\text{Answer: Horizontal reflection and vertical dilation}$

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs of transformations does NOT commute?

options.text: Vertical dilation by factor $5$ and vertical translation down by $4$
Horizontal translation left by $2$ and vertical translation up by $5$
options.why: Horizontal and vertical translations act on different axes and commute.

options.text: Reflection across the $y$-axis and reflection across the $x$-axis
options.why: Reflections across perpendicular axes act on independent variables and commute.

options.text: Reflection across the $y$-axis and horizontal dilation by factor $3$
options.why: Reflections and dilations along the same axis commute with each other.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{A dilation and a translation along the same axis do not commute.}$
$\text{Answer: Vertical dilation by factor } 5 \text{ and vertical translation down by } 4$

questions.question_text: The curve $y = 2^x$ is vertically dilated by factor $3$, then translated $5$ units up. What is the resulting equation?

options.why: Multiplied the constant $5$ by $3$, corresponding to translating first then dilating.
Applied the translation horizontally in the exponent instead of vertically.
Applied the dilation factor horizontally into the exponent.

questions.question_text: The graph of $y = x^3$ is translated $2$ units down, then vertically dilated by a factor of $4$. What is the resulting equation?

options.why: Failed to multiply the vertical shift by the dilation factor $4$.
Treated the vertical translation as a horizontal shift inside the cubing function.
Squared the dilation factor on the leading term.

questions.question_text: The graph of $y = \sqrt{x}$ is translated $5$ units to the right, then horizontally dilated by a factor of $\dfrac{1}{3}$. What is the resulting equation?

options.why: Corresponds to dilating first then translating right by $5$ units.
Substituted $\dfrac{x}{3}$ instead of $3x$ for a horizontal dilation factor of $\dfrac{1}{3}$.
Added $5$ instead of subtracting $5$ for a translation to the right.

questions.question_text: To transform $y = f(x)$ into $y = f(5x + 35)$, a student dilates the graph horizontally by a factor of $\dfrac{1}{5}$ first. What translation must be applied next?

options.why: Used the unfactored constant $35$ without dividing by the coefficient $5$.
Shifted to the right instead of to the left for $+35$.
Shifted in the wrong direction and did not divide by $5$.

questions.solution_text:
$f(x) \to f(5x)$
$f(5x) \to f(5(x + 7)) = f(5x + 35)$
$\text{Translate } 7 \text{ units to the left}$

questions.question_text: To transform $y = f(x)$ into $y = f(6x - 18)$, a student translates the graph horizontally first, then dilates horizontally by a factor of $\dfrac{1}{6}$. What was the first translation?

options.why: Divided by $6$ before translating, which is the shift when dilating first.
Shifted to the left instead of to the right for $-18$.
Divided by $6$ and shifted in the wrong direction.

questions.solution_text:
$f(x) \to f(x - 18) \to f(6x - 18)$
$\text{Translate } 18 \text{ units to the right}$

questions.question_text: The parabola $y = x^2$ has vertex $(0,0)$. Transformation 1 translates $8$ units right, then horizontally dilates by factor $\dfrac{1}{4}$. Transformation 2 horizontally dilates by factor $\dfrac{1}{4}$, then translates $8$ units right. What are the respective coordinates of the resulting vertices?

options.why: Swapped the resulting vertices between the two transformation sequences.
Multiplied $8$ by $4$ instead of dividing by $4$ in Transformation 1.
Assumed horizontal dilation and horizontal translation commute.

questions.question_text: To transform $y = f(x)$ into $y = f(10 - 2x)$, a sequence begins with a reflection across the $y$-axis followed by a translation. What translation is required before the final horizontal dilation by $\dfrac{1}{2}$ is applied?

options.why: Divided by $2$ too early before the horizontal dilation was performed.
Substituted $x+10$ into $f(-x)$ which yields $f(-x-10)$ rather than $f(10-x)$.
Used $5$ units left instead of $10$ units right.

questions.solution_text:
$f(x) \to f(-x) \to f(-(x - 10)) = f(10 - x) \to f(10 - 2x)$
$\text{Translate } 10 \text{ units to the right}$

questions.question_text: The hyperbola $y = \dfrac{1}{x}$ has vertical asymptote $x = 0$. Sequence 1 translates $5$ units right then horizontally dilates by factor $4$. Sequence 2 horizontally dilates by factor $4$ then translates $5$ units right. What is the difference between the vertical asymptote positions of Sequence 1 and Sequence 2?

options.text: $15$ units, with Sequence 1 at $x = 20$ and Sequence 2 at $x = 5$

options.why: Assumed the two operations commute and give the same asymptote.

options.text: $5$ units, with Sequence 1 at $x = 10$ and Sequence 2 at $x = 5$
options.why: Added $5$ instead of multiplying by $4$ in Sequence 1.

options.text: $15$ units, with Sequence 1 at $x = 5$ and Sequence 2 at $x = 20$
options.why: Reversed the asymptote locations of Sequence 1 and Sequence 2.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Sequence 1: } x = 0 \to x = 5 \to x = 5 \times 4 = 20$
$\text{Sequence 2: } x = 0 \to x = 0 \to x = 5$
$\text{Difference} = 20 - 5 = 15 \text{ units}$
